reconcile.note: Gill treats patriarchal polygamy as a tolerated departure from Genesis 2's one-flesh marriage, not a divine endorsement, and reads Paul's 'one wife' rule as binding on all.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells lines up Solomon's seven hundred wives, Gideon's many wives, and Jacob's two wives against Genesis 2:24's one-flesh marriage and the Pastoral requirement that a bishop have only one wife, framing it as an unresolved conflict over what marriage Scripture sanctions.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013).

sides.snippet: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.
sides.verseText: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.

sides.snippet: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines
sides.verseText: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his wives turned away his heart.
